_comment: Hand-curated stepwise onboarding flows. Includes common_pitfalls keyed off the AILANG syntax gotchas surfaced during M-AGENT-MCP execution. Update when the language adds/changes a footgun.

agent.audience: AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Continue, Gemini CLI, etc.) picking up AILANG for the first time within a user's session

steps.title: Verify or install AILANG
actions: Run `ailang --version` first — if it succeeds, skip to step 2
If not installed, call `install_guide(harness=<your-harness>)` for the right install command
Re-run `ailang --version` to confirm the install

steps.title: Confirm the remote MCP is connected
actions: If you can call this onboarding_guide tool, the remote MCP is working — skip the rest of this step
Otherwise, point your harness at https://mcp.ailang.sunholo.com/mcp/ (transport: streamable-http)
For Claude Desktop specifically, use the mcp-remote bridge: `npx -y mcp-remote https://mcp.ailang.sunholo.com/mcp/`

steps.title: Load the current syntax
actions: Call `prompt_get(forVersion="", kind="agent")` for the agent-shaped prompt (~180 lines) — start here for any new task
Call `prompt_get(forVersion="", kind="")` only when you need the full ~50 KB reference
Use the prompt as the source of truth for syntax — do NOT guess

steps.title: Discover stdlib + examples before writing code
actions: Call `stdlib_modules(forVersion="")` to see what's available (35 modules)
Call `stdlib_search(query="<keyword>", forVersion="")` to find a function by name/signature/keyword
Call `examples_for_concept(concept="<feature>", forVersion="")` for a working pattern matching the user's task

steps.title: Check limitations + effects before proposing solutions
actions: Call `limitations_list(category="", forVersion="")` if your plan involves recursion-heavy or mutable patterns — AILANG has design constraints (no Y-combinator, etc.)
Call `effects_catalog(forVersion="")` to find the right capability flag for any side-effecting code

steps.title: Write the code
actions: Always start with `module <project>/<file>` declaration (use UNDERSCORES, not hyphens)
Use `${var}` for string interpolation, NOT `++` (which is list-only — see common_pitfalls)
Declare effects in the function signature: `! {IO, FS}` etc.
For the eval-harness: use `module benchmark/solution`

steps.title: Type-check then run
actions: `ailang check file.ail` — type-check first (fast feedback)
`ailang run --caps IO,FS --entry main file.ail` — flags MUST come BEFORE the filename (silent failure otherwise)
On error: call `examples_for_concept` for a working analog, or call `submit_feedback` to file a docs/bug report

steps.title: When stuck — submit feedback
actions: Call `submit_feedback(title, body, category="bug"|"feature"|"docs"|"limitation", ailang_version, snippet, contact)` from inside this MCP session
Lands in the team's public-feedback inbox; counts as a real signal for what blocks agents
Anonymous is fine — provide `contact` only if you want a follow-up

common_pitfalls.note: ++ is list-only in AILANG. Use string interpolation.
Don't use `module` as a parameter name. Pick `name`/`path`/`pkg`.
Hyphens parse as subtraction in module paths. Use underscores. (Directories CAN have hyphens; only the `module` declaration matters.)
Flags after the filename are silently ignored. Always put flags FIRST.
Functions calling println/readLine/file ops MUST declare their effects.

common_pitfalls.right: if validCategory(c) then false else true   -- write a helper, or invert the branches
common_pitfalls.note: AILANG has no `!` for boolean negation. Invert the branches or write a named helper.

agent.verification_path: After step 7, you should have a working .ail file that prints something. If not, call submit_feedback with category=docs and what blocked you — that's the highest-value signal we receive.

developer.audience: Human developer wanting to write AILANG code at the CLI, with or without an AI agent

steps.title: Install AILANG
actions: Quick path: `git clone https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang && cd ailang && make install`
Or grab a release tarball from https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/releases/latest
Verify: `ailang --version`

steps.title: Try the REPL
actions: `ailang repl` — interactive evaluator, no module declaration needed
Try: `5 + 3`, then `:type 5`, then `:help`

steps.title: Read the prompt for syntax
actions: `ailang prompt` — the canonical teaching prompt (full ~50 KB)
`ailang prompt --compact` — the smaller variant (~15 KB)
`ailang prompt --source mcp` — fetch fresher version from the remote MCP if available

steps.title: Browse examples
actions: `ailang examples list` — all working examples
`ailang examples search "effects"` — find by keyword
`ailang examples show adt_option --run` — view + execute

steps.title: Write your first program
actions: Create a file with `module hello/main` declaration
Use the syntax from `ailang prompt`; copy patterns from examples
Type-check: `ailang check hello.ail`
Run: `ailang run --caps IO --entry main hello.ail`

steps.title: Add an AI agent (optional)
actions: Install ailang_bootstrap for your harness (Claude Code / Gemini CLI / Codex CLI) — see install_guide
Or just add the remote MCP `https://mcp.ailang.sunholo.com/mcp/` to whatever harness you use
Now your agent has typed AILANG knowledge tools

steps.title: Z3 verification (optional, for proof-curious)
actions: Add `requires`/`ensures` contracts to pure functions
Run `ailang verify file.ail` to discharge contracts via Z3
Read the Z3 patterns: call `docs_search(query="verification")` via MCP

steps.title: Get unstuck
actions: REPL `:help` for inline commands
`ailang docs std/<module>` for stdlib reference
https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/issues for bugs
Or call submit_feedback via MCP for a quick docs/bug report

common_pitfalls.note: Flags after the filename are silently ignored.
Effects MUST be declared in the function signature.

developer.verification_path: After step 5, you should have a runnable .ail file. The REPL and `ailang examples` are the fastest ways to learn the syntax.
